Subject: PrivPool spike-proofing & rack oversubscription 'surgery' — sizing audit

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this on. We're kicking off the private deployment sizing run for our west-coast region and want a pragmatic, spike-proof plan before we sign on the dotted line. High-level profile below — attaching a 7-day p95/p99 traffic trace (see separate upload).

What we need from Redwood: a sizing and topology recommendation (GPU count, warm-pool sizing, headroom calc), clear autoscale + admission thresholds, and a mutual action plan (MAP) so Procurement can align on any SLA/commitment changes.

Current constraints / asks:
- Steady-state: ~2k inference QPS (mixed text generation + chat embeddings), typical 256 token generation windows.
- Spike model: up to 10k QPS for 3–5 minutes during predictable events (product launches).
- Target latency: 99th <= 120ms for gen path, 95th <= 40ms for embeddings.
- Network/rack constraints: hosting partner enforces a 2:1 rack NIC oversubscription; max egress per rack 60Gbps.
- Security: VPC-only, private control-plane, no public egress for request payloads.
- Warmup tolerance: we can accept warmup windows up to 6 minutes but want minimal cold-start impact.

Three things we'd like you to evaluate explicitly:
1) Rack-level oversubscription impact on sustained vs burst throughput and recommended NIC/cross-rack routing.
2) Admission-control policy examples and preferred fallback model variants for graceful degradation (costly model -> smaller quantized variant).
3) Required headroom / warm-pool sizing to avoid SLA breaks during 5-min spikes.

I'll loop in infra once you have a proposal. Timeline: we'd love a preliminary read by EOD Friday (29 Aug) to unblock procurement.

Attachments: acme_7day_trace.json (uploaded), service expectation spreadsheet (separate).

Cheers,
Sophie Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Cloud

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask and the trace. Forwarding internal notes and an initial topology sketch (privgpu_topology_v2.pdf) — this is intentionally conservative and focuses on predictable failure modes under rack oversubscription. High-level read below.

Summary (quick):
- Baseline compute recommendation: 24x H100-80GB-equivalent GPUs distributed across 3 racks (8 GPUs/rack) for the stated steady-state + 40% headroom. This assumes model quantization to int8 for the embeddings path and fp16/amp for the gen path.
- Burst handling: we propose a warm-pool sized to absorb ~20% of a 10k QPS spike (i.e., ~2k QPS equivalent pre-warmed serving capacity) + admission thresholds that shed non-critical workloads (background reranks) to protect gen SLA.
- Network: because the partner enforces 2:1 oversubscription, we suggest cross-rack routing for burst traffic and configuring per-tenant egress policing at the top-of-rack (ToR) with token-bucket shaping. Also recommend using an L4-aware ingress proxy that can route high-p95 requests to less saturated racks.
- Admission & fallback: admission controller with three tiers — green (full model), amber (quantized fallback), red (degraded token-limit + queued responses). We'll include specific threshold numbers in the MAP.

Open clarifying asks for Acme (short):
- Confirm fraction of throughput that is embeddings vs generation (ballpark percent split).
- Confirm acceptable tail-latency for degraded mode (we used 250ms p99 for red mode in our sims).
- Do you have a preferred GPU family? We can size for A100 or H100; H100 shortens queueing but is costlier.

Planned deliverables by EOD Fri (29 Aug):
- Sizing matrix (runway_calculator_v1.xlsx) with per-rack GPU counts and headroom scenarios.
- Admission policy draft and explicit threshold examples.
- Topology PDF (attached) with cross-rack routing diagram and ToR shaping recommendations.
- Short MAP doc with procurement checkpoints + DocuSign link for updated SLA (if needed).

Action items for us: Jonas will model kernel/runtime latency tradeoffs, Karthik will run headroom sims with your real trace.

I'll sync with infra on Friday morning for any final topology clarifications.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

> Summary (quick):
> - Baseline compute recommendation: 24x H100-80GB-equivalent GPUs distributed across 3 racks (8 GPUs/rack) for the stated steady-state + 40% headroom.

Quick technical add:
- GPU family tradeoffs: H100 (H200 depending on availability) gives ~25–35% better per-token throughput on decoder-only generation for long-context workloads due to transformer kernel improvements. If Acme is very sensitive to p99 tail, recommend H100; if cost is primary, A100 with a slightly higher warm pool is acceptable.
- Quantization path: embeddings -> int8 gives large QPS win for very low latency; gen path should use mixed precision plus KV cache pinning to reduce re-compute. We'll call out required memory per model variant in the sizing sheet.
- Networking: ToR shaping + cross-rack routing is correct; add an eBPF-based SYNQ limiter at the ToR for quick shedding of abusive patterns during launch spikes.

I've pushed a small simulation result to the Drive link (see related_links). Karthik — can you validate the run with the 5-min spike windows and update the runway spreadsheet with simulated percent-SLA-violations for each headroom scenario?

-Jonas
